note: browser drive: the two planes seated on the untouched generation and the straighten slider taken all of the way

frame.note: Model root frame, unscaled: the file's own coordinates with the scene graph flattened. The body runs along z; the head is ASSUMED to be at the high end — the bounding box picks the axis and cannot pick the end, so nothing decided this and `forwardEarned` is false. Check it before reading any fraction below: `span.baseHeadFraction`, `span.tipHeadFraction` and every other "back from the nose" reading are measured from whichever end this names, and invert with it. The bend itself does not — it is a turn about an axle through `span.base` and names no end. The span does not have to follow that axis — it is two points on the animal — but "up", "lateral" and "how far back from the nose" are measured in this frame.

span.note: Two points on the body. Both cuts are square to the line between them, that line is the span's direction, and its length is the distance between them. The bend is anchored at `base`, and both points are where the geometry reading's traces start. "trace" is the automatic seat — the body's own centre near where the end was asked for — and "manual" is a reviewer who put it there by hand.

planes.note: Two planes, one at each end of the span, each named by the direction the creature’s axis line runs through it **as the body actually is**. baseNormal is where it runs in and is a pure reference — nothing behind the base cut moves under any bend; tipNormal is where it runs out. apartDegrees (= apartBeforeDegrees, one measurement under the name a reader comparing it with the one below will look for) is how far apart the two stand before any bend, which is the whole of what straightening this run would turn through. apartAfterDegrees is how far apart they are once the bend has carried the tip plane, measured rather than assumed: it is nought at a straighten of 1, which is the contract. tipRest is the body’s own heading there as last measured off the trace, which differs from tipNormal only where a reviewer aimed the plane by hand; restApartDegrees is that heading against the base plane. tipCarried is tipNormal turned by the applied rotation — the front plane where the slider has put it.

straighten.note: How much of the straightening is applied. 0 leaves the body as it is, 1 carries the tip plane onto the base plane so the two are parallel and the run between them is straight, past 1 overshoots and below 0 bends it further the way the animal already goes. turn.appliedDegrees is this times turn.fullDegrees, about axis.vector.

axis.note: The axle the span turns about, through span.base: the shortest rotation carrying planes.tipNormal onto planes.baseNormal, so it is derived from the two planes rather than dialled, and it does not change with straighten.amount. A positive turn carries the body towards axis.up. twistDegrees is how far it leans along the span, which is the share of an oblique aim that is a twist of the span about its own length rather than a bend; it is reported rather than clamped, because clamping it would mean the turn no longer carried the tip plane where it was aimed. vectorBlenderZUp is the same direction in a Z-up armature frame ([x, −z, y]).

turn.note: fullDegrees is the whole straightening the two planes stand apart by; appliedDegrees is straighten.amount of it, which is what the body was actually turned through, and totalDegrees is that same number under the name earlier schemas used. The turn is spread linearly across the span, so the rotation at the base cut is exactly identity and there is no kink there. Its sign is the slider’s; which way round the body goes at a positive amount is carried by axis.vector, which does not flip with it.

reading.windowNote: The geometry reading traces the body's own centre outward from each end of the span, over 26% of the body, following the body rather than a coordinate: each step takes only what is within 2% of the body of where the trace stood one step back, so a limb that reaches past the head is left behind rather than averaged into it.

geometry.baseReference: the body's traced centre over the 26% behind the base cut
geometry.tipReference: the body's traced centre over the 26% ahead of the tip cut
geometry.residualNote: How far each trace sits off its own fitted line, over that run's length. A run of body is nearly a line, so a small figure means the trace followed one thing; past about 0.05 it wandered, and the angle it reports is between two directions nothing in the animal actually runs in.

reading.note: Every angle is measured between two named references and nothing else. inPlaneDegrees is the part of the turn the bend axis accounts for and is what an edit changes; offPlaneDegrees is what the plane does not hold, and a large one means the axis is aimed wrong rather than that the bend is small. A reference that moves with the bend sits inside the span, so "after" less "before" is not turn.totalDegrees — and is larger than it where that reference sits well off the span's own line.

jointsNote: The joints of the chain that lie inside the span, plus the first one past it, in chain order. `local` is the step from the joint above it, which is what a pose bone's own rotation is; `accumulated` is the rotation at that joint's station, which is the product down the chain. Both are about axis.vectorBlenderZUp in an armature whose bones share one rest orientation. This is the shape `uncurl` returns and `carry_rest` consumes in tools/triassic/creatures/askeptosaurus/build.py.

pinch.note: The smallest the inside of the bend is squeezed to, as a fraction of its own length. 1 is no squeeze; below 0 the turn is tighter than the body is thick and the surface has folded through itself.

rule: A vertex at fraction s through the span (its distance from span.base along span.direction, over span.length) is carried to the bent centreline at s and turned about axis.vector by turn.appliedDegrees·s, which is straighten.amount times the angle the two planes stand apart. Behind the base cut s is 0 and nothing moves; past the tip cut s is 1 and the far part is carried rigidly. See docs/viewer-bend.md.
